# Synapse 2.1.1

Every fix since 2.1.0, from runs that say when what they made is empty or cut short to Synapse AI reading the pages you name and making a knowledge base with its pages in one press. Synapse also starts again after a restart unless you say no, and `synapse stop` stops everything it started.

## Changed

- **Synapse starts again after a restart unless you say no.** The installer's question now defaults to Yes (off in CI, containers, or without a service manager, and it says why). On Linux it asks to start at boot without a password, never with sudo, and `synapse autostart off` undoes only what it turned on. An upgrade keeps your choice and never asks again. If Linux won't let it start at boot, it starts when you log in and prints the `sudo loginctl enable-linger` line that lets it start at boot; macOS and Windows start it when you log in.
- **A tool can ask first unless it only reads.** The agent editor's tool policy has a new choice for one tool, Ask unless it only reads: the tool runs when it says it only reads and asks first otherwise, decided each time it runs.
- **Synapse AI can offer a workflow to MCP clients, or stop.** Each workflow has its own Offer to MCP clients switch, but Synapse AI couldn't set it, and when asked it said the only way was Settings › MCP server, which connects a client and offers nothing. Ask it now and it puts up a card, "Offer "Invoice triage" to MCP clients" or "Stop offering … to MCP clients", which you press; the MCP server help names the workflow's own switch.
- **A saved model the builder pickers leave out is headed "Your saved model".** A model Synapse AI isn't offered for building with sat under the heading "Not for building", a verdict on the model, where a picker's only mark is Recommended. Its heading is now "Your saved model", and its line still says it isn't offered for building with Synapse AI and to pick a Recommended model.
- **The model pickers order the models measured for building by how they did.** Claude Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5 and Haiku 5.5 and Gemini 3 Flash were measured building two real asks (a third, changing an existing form, was not measured). Among models of the same tier, the measured ones now follow how they did, so Haiku 4.5 comes before Haiku 5.5; a measure never moves a model past a stronger tier and never marks one Recommended.

## Fixed

- **A model step reads the whole of a long input.** A step's input keys cut each value at 5,000 characters, whatever its model could read, so a step revising a long draft saw its start and its end and wrote placeholders for the middle, or rewrote it. An input key now holds a value up to what the step's model can read, and never less than before, as a `{{ state.x }}` reference does.
- **An agent hands on what it found.** An Agent step whose answer a later step reads is now told that its answer is all that step gets. When its answer is far shorter than what its tools returned, such as a one-line status after reading a site, the step warns, naming both sizes, so the next step is not left to guess.
- **A step that can't read files sees what it can of a long value.** A value too long for a step's prompt is saved as a file, and an LLM step was given only the file's name and a tool it doesn't have to read it. It now gets the start of the value, as much as fits, and is told how much is not shown and that an Agent step can read all of it.
- **A step that would read a page it can't take in whole is said before it runs.** An LLM step reading a page, a crawl or a file a Tool step fetched can be handed more than it can read, and then gets only part of it. Checking a workflow now says so, naming the step and the fix (make it an Agent step, which can read the whole file, or have it read only the part it needs), and Synapse AI plans such a step as an Agent step.
- **A tool of an app that isn't connected right now is kept, not refused.** When an app you set up was asleep, down or waiting to be signed in again as you built, each of its tools read as one nothing provides: a check failed the workflow, an agent couldn't be given the tool, and Synapse AI offered to connect an app you already had. Such a tool is now kept with a warning that it can't be checked right now, and why, and a scheduled run never waits on a choice made while the app was down.
- **Synapse AI speaks as itself.** When you asked it to build something but it read your message as a question, Synapse AI could answer with the name of one of its internal parts and say it couldn't build. It now speaks as Synapse AI and says how to ask for the build, which it drafts as a plan for you to check.
- **A long wait on the model says what is happening.** When a model call doesn't answer in time and is asked again, the waiting line now says so for as long as the wait goes on. A Synapse AI turn whose model never answered says so plainly and what to try next (try again, ask for a smaller part, or pick another model), instead of the provider's error text.
- **A large plan is no longer cut off while it is being written.** Asked for a complex workflow on Claude, Synapse AI's planner could spend its whole answer allowance thinking, and a call that took longer than three minutes was cut and sent again on every try, so the build waited about sixteen minutes and then failed. Each call now has the time to write what it is allowed to, and Claude models that think as they go have room for their thinking and an answer.
- **A page you name is read and answered in the chat.** Asked to read a page you gave the address of and tell you about it, such as a summary, a comparison or what it says, Synapse AI said it couldn't read a page in the chat and offered to build a workflow that would, and asked where to send the result. It now reads those pages and answers in the chat, once. An ask to do it again, send it somewhere or build it still goes to a plan, and a page that needs a sign-in, or would not load, is said plainly.
- **Synapse AI says only the signed-in sessions you have.** Asked to read a page behind a sign-in, Synapse AI could talk of a saved session for that site as if one were ready, and give a reason for not reading the page that wasn't the real one. It now knows which sites the browser keeps a session for: a Browser agent can use those, any other site needs you to sign in to it once under Agents › Browser › Sessions, and a page it read that asked for a sign-in is said as that.
- **A run says when what it made is empty, partial or a CSV with no rows.** A run that read a long page got only its first 50,000 characters, found none of the rows it wanted in them, wrote a CSV holding only its header, and said "completed". Now a step whose answer the page reader cut short says how much of it was read, a step that made nothing says its result is empty, and a step that writes a CSV with only its header says so. Each warning is in the run's log and on the step, and the run reads "Completed with warnings", its hover naming the steps. A field the workflow says may be empty is never warned about.
- **A workflow's first run reads a file it hasn't written yet as empty.** A workflow that reads a Vault file and later writes it, such as one that compares a price with the last one it saved, failed on its first run because the file wasn't there yet. Synapse AI now plans such a read to find nothing on the first run and says so on the plan, the Vault read takes `missing_ok` for that, and checking a workflow points such a read out with its fix. A read of a file that no step writes still fails when the file is missing.
- **Synapse AI offers to build something once, and a yes builds it.** A reply that already offered to build a workflow got a second, near-identical offer after it, and a reply that asked "Shall I go ahead and plan this out?" got nothing done when you said yes. Now an offer is made once, and saying yes to one Synapse AI made builds what you asked for.
- **A plan gives one page limit for a site it reads.** A plan that builds a knowledge base by reading a website could say "up to 500 pages" on its step and "up to 50 pages" under What I assumed. It now gives the one limit the reading is held to.
- **Synapse AI makes a knowledge base with its pages and a board with its cards.** Asked for a knowledge base of a web page, its card made an empty base and the page was refused as if the base didn't exist; asked for a board with cards, the cards were refused the same way. Now the card that makes a knowledge base names the pages it is filled from, the card that makes a board names its first cards, and one press makes it with them. Anything else asked for the new base or board is said as coming once it is made.
- **A feature that is off is said once.** Asked for several things that need Boards while Boards were off, Synapse AI put up the "Turn on Boards" card once for each, with the same sentence each time. It now says it once, with one switch.
- **Claude Code's model names say what they run.** In the model pickers, Claude Code's short names (haiku, sonnet, opus, fable) had no line under them, though the full model names beside them did. Each now shows the facts of the model Claude Code runs for it today, such as its context window.
- **`synapse stop` stops everything Synapse started.** The web server no longer keeps running after it says stopped, a stopped process is never called 'Failed to stop', a stale pidfile never stops another program, and it says so in two lines.
- **A knowledge base says why it couldn't read a site's robots.txt.** A site whose robots.txt timed out was reported as one that couldn't be read, the same as a site that was down. Knowledge now says which it was: the file timed out (and after how long), the site didn't answer, it answered a server error, or the file is larger than SynapseBot reads. The page is tried again at the next crawl.
- **A page with no words of its own is never indexed.** A page built by JavaScript could be indexed as nothing but its "Skip to main content" link. Knowledge now leaves such a page out and says it may need JavaScript to render. A short page with real text, or a heading that only starts like a skip link, is still indexed.
- **A page behind a sign-in, or one that isn't there, is never read as the page you asked for.** A web read that landed on a site's sign-in page handed back the login form, and a read of a missing page handed back the site's "not found" page, each as the page's content. Both the scraper and Knowledge now say "Needs a sign-in" or "The page is not there (HTTP 404)". A page that loads and only talks about signing in or about 404s is still read.
- **A site's bot protection is named, and Knowledge fetches as a polite reader.** When a protection service refuses SynapseBot, Knowledge now says whose it is (Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome and others) and the way on: add the page as a file, or connect a scraping service with your own key. SynapseBot never takes a browser check. Its requests now carry a reader's Accept headers, and a site that asks it to wait 30 seconds or less is asked once more after that wait. A longer wait is named and the page is tried at the next crawl.
- **A link Synapse AI gives into the docs lands on its section.** The docs index Synapse AI searches gave about 125 headings an anchor the docs site doesn't use: a heading with its own id, a heading used twice on one page, or one with code in it. So a cited link opened at the top of the page or on the wrong section. Every anchor is now the one the docs page gives that heading.
- **Synapse AI says which model apps are signed in, and how to sign in to the rest.** Asked which models it could use, Synapse AI said a signed-in Claude Code's models were there "if you have a Claude CLI session signed in", and didn't mention the apps installed but not signed in. It now says the signed-in ones' models can be used, and names each one that isn't signed in with how to sign in.
- **Synapse AI gives each model's own context window and price.** Asked which models it could use, Synapse AI could give one window for a whole family ("all Claude models have 200K"), where Fable 5 and Opus 5 read 1M. It now reads each model's window and price from the model picker's own list: a model app's price is its subscription, a local model is free, and what isn't known isn't said.
- **What you read never carries Synapse AI's own internal id.** Asked to answer from a knowledge base it had just set up, Synapse AI tried to ask an agent named by its own internal id, and the reply said there was no agent by that id, with a hint written for its own use. It now says in plain words that it is Synapse AI itself, and a line written for its own use (where to read names from, a kind written as its code name) never reaches what you read.
- **A knowledge base a plan makes is one something reads.** A plan could list a knowledge base and make an agent "to answer from it" without giving the agent the base or a step that searches it, so the agent answered from nothing. The plan check now sends such a plan back with how to put it right: give the base to the agent that answers from it, add a step that searches it, or drop it.
- **A start you ask for is made, or said.** Asked for a workflow that starts "when a new email reaches the support inbox", a plan was built to start only when someone runs it, and its card never said the start you asked for was gone. A plan now says how you asked it to start and how it does, on a schedule, from a form, or, when that can't be done here, why and what starts it instead, under Missing here.
- **A plan never assumes what a tool answers.** Asked for the humidity, a plan read a weather tool's answer and assumed it held humidity, though the tool says it answers only the city and the temperature; the run then said, honestly, that there was none. A step that reads a tool's whole answer now names the fields it uses, and a field the tool doesn't list goes back to the planner, to use a field it has, find a tool that answers it, or say the part can't be done.
- **The editor's Save is never under the other bar.** With something to check, a Board, Last run and a long name, the bar at the top right of the canvas could cover Save, most often on a phone, so a click on Save landed on Run and only Ctrl+S saved. When the two bars don't fit, the right one now shows its icons alone, and then moves to a line of its own; Save stays where a click reaches it.
- **A website widget a build doesn't make is never said to be made.** Asked for a website chat widget, a build made the agent and its knowledge base and its card said "a website chat widget" under You asked for, but no widget was made. A widget is made on its own card once its agent exists, so the plan now says the widget isn't made here, and how to make it: ask for a website widget for that agent, or make one under Widgets.
- **A table or list from a very long page is read whole, or said as too large.** Asked for a table or list from a very long page, Synapse AI planned a read that keeps only its first 50,000 characters, so the rows past it were lost. It now reads such a page whole from its table, or says the page is too large for one read and what it can do instead. Its read of a page it plans with says it is SynapseBot and obeys the site's robots.txt.
- **The web scraper says what it does with a site that says no.** Its description said it handles anti-bot protections. It now says what it does: a page behind a bot check, a sign-in or a 404 fails with the reason.

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.1.1`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.1.0 or 2.0.x:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first. An upgrade keeps your start-after-restart choice and never asks again; `synapse autostart status` says which you have, and `synapse autostart on` or `off` changes it.
- **`synapse stop` prints two lines:** "Stopping Synapse..." and then "Synapse stopped.", "Synapse was not running." or "Could not stop: …". A script that read its old line per process should read the second line.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.

**Full changelog:** [v2.1.0...v2.1.1](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/compare/v2.1.0...v2.1.1) · [Documentation](https://docs.synapseorch.com)
